meta.title: Language tree — every family our people groups belong to, coloured by what the gospel sources hold
meta.citation: Hammarström, Harald & Forkel, Robert & Haspelmath, Martin & Bank, Sebastian. 2025. Glottolog 5.2.1. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. (Available online at https://glottolog.org)
meta.newick_note: Glottolog publishes every subtree in Newick (text/newick), the standard text format for trees; this file is its drawing, with the classification path kept as parent links.

colours.g: a New Testament or full Bible found in the language (eBible nt/full, or a resource scoped New Testament / Full Bible / 27 or 66 parts: FCBH, Scripture Earth, PNG.Bible, Door43)
colours.y: something found in the language (film, audio, stories, portions) but no New Testament
colours.r: nothing found in the language in the sources checked; never a claim that nothing exists
colours.parent: a family or branch shows the WORST colour inside it, with counts, so the gap is what the eye finds
colours.dialect: every source catalogues by LANGUAGE (ISO 639-3), never by dialect: a dialect carries its language's colour (inh:1) and is drawn lighter

meta.collapsed: chains of single-child branches are drawn as one link; the skipped names are in `via`
